_doc: Agents in Situationship — 20 modern-dating scenarios. Each scenario has 4 lettered options. The judge sums per-trait weights across all 20 answers, detects 'disorganized' attachment via 3 consistency probe pairs, and derives a viral label. There is no canonical 'correct' answer — the case is graded on FORMAT only. The derived attachment_style, flavor_traits, and label are surfaced as metadata.

questions.text: They read your message 8 hours ago and haven't replied, but just posted a story.

A.text: No worries, hope your day's going well :)

B.text: Say nothing and wait.

C.text: Saw you were online lol

D.text: All good. Let's catch up another time.

questions.text: You sent a long voice message last night. They replied 'k' this morning.

A.text: Send another voice message asking if everything's okay.

B.text: 'Lol fair, talk later.' Move on with your day.

C.text: Don't reply. Leave them on read.

D.text: 'Did I say something wrong?'

questions.text: They cancelled plans 3 weekends in a row, each time with a believable excuse.

A.text: Plan the next weekend yourself and double-confirm.

B.text: 'Hey, I've noticed a pattern. Are we okay?'

C.text: Stop initiating. See what they do.

D.text: Cancel on them next time without warning.

questions.text: You see them online actively typing to you, then 'typing...' stops and no message arrives.

B.text: Wait, they probably needed to think.

C.text: Screenshot it and send it to your group chat.

D.text: Pretend you didn't notice and bring it up later, casually.

questions.text: They said 'I miss you' 4 days ago and haven't suggested meeting up since.

B.text: Suggest a specific time and place.

C.text: 'Cool' and leave it.

D.text: Re-read the 'miss you' 12 times and decide they're cheating.

questions.text: Your situationship just changed their bio from '🌹' to '—'.

B.text: Wonder what it means for an hour, then ask a friend.

C.text: Ask them directly: 'the new bio mean anything?'

D.text: Change yours to match.

questions.text: They text 'we need to talk' with no other context.

B.text: Don't reply for hours.

C.text: Spiral for 6 hours, then reply 'okay'.

D.text: 'About what.'

questions.text: They want to 'define the relationship.' You like them but you're not sure.

B.text: Be honest about your hesitation, in detail.

C.text: Agree to whatever they want, panic later.

D.text: End it preemptively before they can bring it up again.

questions.text: They left a hoodie at your place. It's been 3 weeks.

A.text: Wash it, fold it, return it next time you see them.

B.text: Wear it sometimes. Don't bring it up.

C.text: Box it up and mail it back.

D.text: Forget it exists.

questions.text: You've been seeing them for two months. They invite you to their best friend's birthday party.

B.text: Make an excuse.

C.text: Go, but spend the night anxious about how their friends are perceiving you.

D.text: Go, but tell yourself it doesn't mean anything.

questions.text: They asked what you're looking for.

A.text: Tell them honestly, even if it might end things.

B.text: Mirror whatever they say.

C.text: 'Idk man, just vibing.'

D.text: Give a vague answer to keep options open.

questions.text: They suggest hanging out only after midnight. Every single time.

B.text: Go anyway, because at least you're seeing them.

C.text: Stop responding to their late-night texts.

D.text: Match their energy — only text them after midnight.

questions.text: You're at a party. Their ex walks in.

B.text: Watch your situationship like a hawk all night.

C.text: Bring up the ex on the ride home.

D.text: Leave early without explaining why.

questions.text: You see them like a 2019 photo of someone you don't know on Instagram.

B.text: Check that person's entire profile.

C.text: Like an old photo of one of your exes in retaliation.

D.text: Bring it up casually next conversation.

questions.text: Their phone lights up next to you. You see a notification from a name you don't recognize.

B.text: Try to read the preview.

C.text: Ask them who it is.

D.text: Save the name. Google it later.

questions.text: You're at brunch. Mid-meal, you see them texting under the table.

A.text: Don't say anything but make a mental note.

B.text: 'Everything okay?'

C.text: Ask who they're texting.

D.text: Text them under the table from across the table.

questions.text: They tease you in front of their friends in a way that stings.

B.text: Tease them back with the same energy.

C.text: Bring it up privately later.

D.text: Get quiet for the rest of the night.

questions.text: They forgot your birthday. They remember two days late and feel awful.

B.text: Accept the apology but say it hurt.

C.text: 'Yeah.' That's all you say.

D.text: Forgive them out loud, vent to three friends about it.

questions.text: You finally tell them what you want from this thing. They reply: 'let's just enjoy this for now.'

A.text: 'Okay, that works for me.' — even though it doesn't.

B.text: 'Then I think I need to step back.'

C.text: Agree, then start emotionally pulling away without saying so.

D.text: Agree, and silently hope they'll change their mind in a few weeks.

questions.text: It's 2am. They text 'u up?'

B.text: 'It's late, talk tomorrow.'

C.text: Reply 6 hours later: 'sorry just saw this.'

D.text: See it. Don't reply. Stare at the screen for 20 minutes.
